topic.angle: Relay stations made messages travel fast

body.question: Mongol messengers changed horses at relay stations along the road. About how far could they cover in a single day?
body.reveal: Messengers covered 200-300 km per day. Stations roughly 32-64 km apart offered food, shelter and spare horses, and a messenger could hand the message on and rest. Ögedei Khan gave the system special attention because Mongol armies travelled fast and their messengers had to be even faster.

probes.question: What did the yam relay stations provide?
True or false: in the yam system, a messenger could pass the information to another messenger at a station.
